text:
Anya P.: Quick sync—enterprise legal flagged a hard requirement: keep a single-string 'prompt' param for legacy integrations. They want a clear migration path but need immediate compat. Do we accept both 'prompt' and 'messages' in the API, or pick one and offer a server-side shim? Need decision + launch criteria.
Matt H.: I lean accept-both initially. Implement a translation layer in the API that converts prompt -> messages. Simpler for customers, lets us keep messages-first UX long-term.
Kevin L.: Agree accept-both for rollout. Two notes: 1) translation should be deterministic so evals are repeatable. 2) measure runtime cost — parsing is trivial but we must confirm it doesn't affect p95 GPU scheduling where every ms counts.
Samir: UX + SDK work. If we accept both we need clear precedence (if both provided) and show deprecation warnings in SDKs/docs. Also provide helper in SDKs: client.convertPromptToMessages(prompt, systemRole?)
Anya P.: Launch criteria suggestion: must not increase p95 end-to-end latency by >50ms at 99th on hosted API; quality/regression delta vs messages-only must be <1% on our eval prompt set; and migration docs + sample code must be published.
Matt H.: API proposal (minimal): accept payload with either "prompt": string OR "messages": [{"role":"system|user|assistant","content":"..."}]. If both present server chooses messages and logs a warning. Add optional boolean "compat_mode":true for customers who want deterministic legacy behavior.
Kevin L.: Function-calling and structured outputs caveat: tool calling expects role semantics (system instructions, assistant tool outputs). Translation must insert a system role around prompt only if customer explicitly indicates system-level context. Otherwise we risk changing behavior (customers might expect the prompt to be entirely user content). Recommendation: when converting prompt -> messages, wrap as {role: "user", content: prompt} by default, but allow an explicit meta header: "prompt_role_hint": "system|user".
Samir: Docs + examples for SDKs: show three paths—pure messages, pure prompt, and prompt with role_hint. Add migration snippet in multiple languages. Also add deprecation timeline if we ever remove prompt.
Matt H.: Rollout plan: canary (1% traffic, compat_mode enabled) -> 10% after 48h -> 100% after metrics green. Telemetry: track requests using prompt vs messages, avg tokens, p95 latency, and quality regressions via our regression harness.
deploy-bot: deploy initiated: api/compat-shim v1 -> canary -> 1% -> sha: 3f7a2b.
Kevin L.: For quality monitoring: run the prompt->messages converted inputs through our eval set and compare to messages baseline. If mismatch rate >1.0% then block rollout. Also log cases where function-calling behavior differs.
Anya P.: Customer asks also included: enterprise SLA for latency and explicit guidance on how prompt will be logged/audited. We need privacy note in docs: converted prompt should appear in audit logs only if customer opts in.
Samir: Small code snippet for docs to convert prompt client-side (JS):
```js
// migration helper
function promptToMessages(prompt, roleHint = 'user') {
  return [{ role: roleHint, content: prompt }];
}

// usage
const body = prompt ? { prompt } : { messages };
```
Matt H.: Edgecases: very long prompts that exceed typical system message length—should chunk or recommend messages. Also embeddings/rerank workflows: these still accept raw text; ensure we don't accidentally route prompt->messages conversions into embedding pipelines.
Kevin L.: Action items: 1) Eng to prototype translation + telemetry (Matt). 2) ML to run eval regression (Kevin). 3) Devex to draft migration doc & SDK helpers (Samir). 4) Product to finalize launch criteria and timeline (Anya).
Anya P.: Timeline proposal: prototype + evals this week, docs + SDK PRs next week, canary deploy in 2 weeks. If all green, GA end of sprint.
Matt H.: I'll open the RFC PR with the API shape + shim details and include the conversion logic and telemetry counters.
Samir: I'll start a docs draft and add example notebooks for tool-calling + structured output after conversion.
Kevin L.: I'll start running the regression harness now with a small set of customer prompts.
Anya P.: Great—please @me when PRs are up. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
